sections.h2: What should a house seller know about Oklahoma as a whole?
sections.html:
Oklahoma became the 46th state on November 16, 1907, and counted 3,959,353 residents in the 2020 census. Its capital, Oklahoma City, is also its largest city, and the state covers about 69,699 square miles, which ranks 20th among the states.

For a seller, the useful point is that state law sets the property tax calendar, the deed tax and the landlord rules, while counties run the offices where houses are valued, taxed and recorded. A sale in the Panhandle and one in Tulsa follow the same statutes through different local offices.

sections.h2: How is Oklahoma divided into regions and counties?
sections.html:
The state has 77 counties. Most of Oklahoma lies in the Great Plains, Cross Timbers and Interior Highlands, with the Ouachita, Arbuckle, Wichita and Ozark mountain ranges.

The newest county is Cotton, established in 1912, while seven counties date from 1890: Beaver, Canadian, Cleveland, Kingfisher, Logan, Oklahoma and Payne. Osage County is the largest by area at 2,251 square miles.

sections.h2: Which cities and metros anchor the housing market?
sections.html:
Oklahoma City and Tulsa anchor it. Wikipedia's 2010 city counts put Oklahoma City at 579,999, Tulsa at 391,906, Norman at 110,925, Broken Arrow at 98,850 and Lawton at 96,867.

By 2020 the Greater Oklahoma City metro had 1,425,695 people and the Tulsa metro 1,015,331. Together those two metros hold roughly 2.4 million of the state's 3.96 million residents, so the rest of the state is spread across smaller cities and towns.

  • Oklahoma City: the state capital and its largest city, seat of Oklahoma County.
  • Tulsa: the second-largest city, seat of Tulsa County.
  • Norman, Broken Arrow and Lawton: the next three cities by 2010 count.

sections.h2: What drives the Oklahoma economy and why does it matter to a house?
sections.html:
Mining, which includes oil and natural gas, is the largest single sector at about 22.5 percent of state GDP in the first quarter of 2020, according to Wikipedia's economy page. Government comes next at about 13.9 percent, then trade, transportation and utilities.

The largest employers listed for 2019 were the U.S. Department of Defense at about 69,000, Walmart at about 32,200, the University of Oklahoma at about 17,800, the Chickasaw Nation at about 11,300 and the Choctaw Nation at about 10,000. The state page also names energy companies based in Tulsa and an American Airlines maintenance base there.

Housing demand follows these jobs. An energy slowdown, a base assignment or a university cycle can change how long a house sits in a particular town, even when the state taxes stay the same.

sections.h2: What does Oklahoma weather mean for the condition of a house?
sections.html:
Most of Oklahoma is in Tornado Alley, and the state averages 62 tornadoes a year, one of the highest rates in the world. The highest-risk months are April through June.

Winter brings snow, sleet or freezing rain, especially in the east. Temperatures can exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit or drop below zero in much of the state, and rainfall ranges from under 17 inches a year in the Panhandle to more than 40 inches in the southeast.

  • Roofs and siding take the hardest hits from storms.
  • Long hot, dry stretches are common in July and August in many years, which is worth remembering when judging a house in summer.
  • Damaged houses are often sold as is when owners do not want to manage repairs.

sections.h2: How do conditions differ between eastern, central and western Oklahoma?
sections.html:
Climate changes a lot from one end of the state to the other, and that shapes what buyers look for in a house. Wikipedia describes the central, southern and eastern areas as humid subtropical and the western High Plains and Panhandle as semiarid.

Average annual temperature runs about 62 degrees Fahrenheit in the southeast and 58 in the Panhandle. Snowfall averages under 4 inches in the far south and just over 20 inches along the Colorado border in the Panhandle.

The terrain differs too. The state includes the Ouachita, Arbuckle, Wichita and Ozark mountain ranges, its highest point is Black Mesa at 4,974 feet, and its lowest is 289 feet on the Little River. Oklahoma also has more than 200 dam-created lakes, built after the Dust Bowl drought, so a lakeside or rural property can be a very different sale from a city lot.

When a seller is comparing offers, those differences are a reason to read the local county guide before assuming that a statewide rule produces the same result everywhere.

sections.h2: When are Oklahoma property taxes due, and who collects them?
sections.html:
Taxes are due and payable on November 1, and the county treasurer collects them. If at least half is paid before January 1, the rest is due before April 1, and if not, the whole levy becomes delinquent on January 1.

Delinquent tax carries interest of 1.5 percent a month, capped at the unpaid principal amount, and the treasurer can waive penalties incurred through no fault of the taxpayer. Bills of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1.

The county assessor sets valuations, and the Oklahoma Tax Commission's Ad Valorem Division performs an annual equalization study of each county for the State Board of Equalization. Our statewide property tax page covers appeals; the homestead filing is due by March 15.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording rules apply when a house sells?
sections.html:
Oklahoma imposes a documentary stamp tax of $0.75 for each $500 of consideration, or fraction of it, on deeds conveying real estate when the value exceeds $100. Consideration excludes liens or encumbrances that remain on the property, and the tax attaches when the deed is executed and delivered.

Recording gives public notice. Under 16 O.S. 16, a recorded conveyance is constructive notice of its contents to later buyers, mortgage holders and creditors. County clerks hold the land records, and some, like Oklahoma County's, offer a free alert when a document is recorded under your name.

If the house is an exempt homestead, a deed generally needs both spouses' signatures under 16 O.S. 4.

sections.h2: How do the four state topics in this directory connect to a sale?
sections.html:
Each statewide topic answers a different reason a seller might need speed. Which one fits depends on who lives in the house and who owes what.

  • Tenants: the notice periods and court steps in 41 O.S. and 12 O.S. 1148, where a rented house is sold with the tenant in place.
  • Landlords: deposits within 45 days, entry notice and lease transfer on sale.
  • Homeowners: the March 15 homestead filing and the one-acre town limit.
  • Heirs and lenders: the probate, sheriff sale and deed pages on this site.

Seeing which category applies first helps a seller decide whether to read a county page, a city page or a statewide guide next.

faqs.q: How many counties does Oklahoma have?
faqs.a: 77. The most populous are Oklahoma County at 822,125 and Tulsa County at 698,782, and the largest by area is Osage County at 2,251 square miles, according to Wikipedia's list of Oklahoma counties.

faqs.q: When are Oklahoma property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 1. Under 68 O.S. 2913, the whole bill becomes delinquent January 1 unless half has been paid by then, in which case the second half is due before April 1.

faqs.q: How much is the Oklahoma deed tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: $0.75 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it, when the value exceeds $100. Remaining liens or encumbrances are excluded from the consideration, under 68 O.S. 3201.

faqs.q: What are the largest cities in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Oklahoma City is the largest, followed by Tulsa, Norman, Broken Arrow and Lawton, based on the 2010 counts on Wikipedia's Oklahoma page. Greater Oklahoma City and Tulsa were the two largest metros in 2020.

faqs.q: Does Oklahoma have extreme weather that affects houses?
faqs.a: Yes. Most of the state is in Tornado Alley with about 62 tornadoes a year, plus ice storms in the east and long hot, dry spells in summer.

faqs.q: Does state law or the county decide the property tax homestead filing?
faqs.a: Both play a part. State law sets the March 15 deadline and the exemption amounts, while the county assessor receives the application and approves it.
